Tessa —

My take: we should present a two-track option to Northern Bank. Keep the standard SLA as the baseline but offer a pilot-level operational exception that includes explicit responsibilities and a short, measurable target.

Option A (baseline):
- SLA: RTO 60m / RPO 15m (standard multi-region hosted offering).
- Redwood owns warm-standby infrastructure and health monitoring; customer owns application-level verification and acceptance testing.

Option B (pilot exception):
- Agreed pilot window (e.g., 2 months) where Redwood will commit to RTO=30m during US business hours and RPO=10m. This requires dedicated warm-standby sizing and an explicit runbook and incident activation checklist.
- Failover stewardship: Redwood will trigger and execute the technical switchover; Northern Bank will own business verification and release gating. First 60 minutes joint runbook execution: Redwood handles system-level warmup & routing; Northern Bank runs acceptance tests.
- Liability carveout: we add language that the 30m/10m commitment applies only during the pilot window and excludes third-party outages (cloud provider region faults) if they exceed our control plane window.

If they insist on 15m RTO or 5m RPO, we should push back on 5m RPO unless they accept synchronous cross-region replication and cost uplift. I can draft the exception language.

—Marissa
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: Redwood pilot proposal & failover questions

Marissa / Tessa —

Operational note from SRE: engineering can support a pilot-level RTO target of 30 minutes for US business hours with the following constraints and mitigations:

- Warm-standby sizing: we recommend a dedicated warm pool sized to handle 1.2x expected peak QPS for the pilot window. For Northern Bank’s workload that equates to 3x A100 GPUs or equivalent. Warm pool should be reserved and pre-loaded with model weights and a KV prefix cache warmed on a rolling basis.
- Activation steps (high level): issue routing flip (3 min), validate BGP/edge propagation (up to 5–7 min), warm KV cache & prefix replay (5–12 min depending on dataset), health checks & smoke tests (2–3 min). End-to-end expected 20–35 minutes in normal conditions.
- RPO: achieving 5 minutes requires synchronous mirroring of request/transaction data across regions — we do not currently operate synchronous cross-region replication. Our assisted approach can reach ~10 minutes RPO using near-real-time async replication with aggressive flush policies (application-level writes buffered and shipped every 60–120s).
- Runbook/stewardship: we propose Redwood is responsible for technical activation and monitoring for the first 30 minutes. Northern Bank stays on verification channel and confirms business continuity. After 30 minutes, if manual escalation or extended recovery is required, both parties jump to the joint incident execution checklist.

I'll attach standby-sizing-estimate.xlsx with the numbers. If they want 15m RTO guaranteed, we need additional measures (larger pre-warmed pool, faster KV write durability strategies, and explicit test windows) and it would materially increase cost.

—Sean

Hi James / Elena —

Thanks for the questions and patience while we scoped this internally. Based on our engineering readout, here's the proposal we suggest for the pilot and the language we'll include in the SOW:

Agreed pilot terms (30-day trial, convertible to annual contract):
- Pilot SLA (pilot exception): Redwood will operate with a pilot RTO target of 30 minutes during Northern Bank US business hours (Mon–Fri 07:00–19:00 ET).
- Pilot RPO: target 10 minutes using near-real-time async replication (we cannot provide 5-minute RPO without synchronous cross-region replication).
- Failover stewardship: Redwood will trigger and execute the technical failover and routing flip for the first 30 minutes and run system-level verifications. Northern Bank will be the authority for business acceptance and final release gating during verification.
- Scope & carveouts: pilot exception applies only to the specified pilot window and excludes cloud provider region-blackout events beyond our control; we will include a clear incident escalation ladder and runbook in the SOW.
- Operational commitments: Redwood commits to pre-sizing and reserving warm-standby capacity for the pilot (estimated 3x GPU units) and to run quarterly failover drills during the pilot.

Next steps:
1) I'll draft the one-page pilot exception (runbook + stewardship table) and share it by EOD tomorrow for your review.
2) If acceptable, procurement can accept this as an addendum to the SOW and we’ll schedule a kickoff and baseline failover drill in week 2 of the pilot.
